questions.question: As a rider, how can you reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Do not look ahead for hazards.
Do not use turn signals because they distract other drivers.
Make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make yourself visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, signal your moves clearly, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead, and spot hazards early. Always be ready to react to dangers.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Blocks most of your side vision.
Lets you see to the sides enough for safe riding.
Can create danger for the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see to the sides enough for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see everything you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight, so you should:

options.text: Not worry about wearing bright clothing during the day.
Wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight hours. Wear bright colors when riding, even in the daytime, to be more noticeable.

questions.question: Can motorcycle riders share a lane with other vehicles?

options.text: Yes, with cars.
Yes, when traffic is heavy.
No. Riders should use the full lane and not share it with other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Riders should use the full lane and not share it with other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs the entire lane width to operate safely. Riders should never share lanes with other vehicles.

questions.question: When is there less grip available for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is leaning.
When a motorcycle is straight upright.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, there is less grip for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance to four seconds?

options.text: When the pavement is wet from rain or snow.
When the road has more than one lane.
When there is light traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet from rain or snow.
questions.explanation: A three-second following distance is normal, but increase it to four seconds when riding in conditions that need longer stopping distances. Increase your distance on slippery roads.

questions.question: While riding, where should your feet be?

options.text: On the gas tank.
Hanging loose.
On the footrests.

questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you stay balanced.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic light ahead
Intersection ahead
Divided highway ahead

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a divided highway ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, all riders should:

options.text: Check their mirrors often.
Only the lead rider should check mirrors.
Not check mirrors often because it is distracting.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors regularly. This helps you watch the riders behind you and see if the group is staying together.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the driver's blind spot.
You will have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is unsafe because you may be in the driver's blind spot where they cannot see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Has little impact on whether or not other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it may affect whether or not other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it may affect whether or not other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position matters. It helps other drivers see you and helps you see the road ahead. Good positioning also protects you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, you should:

options.text: Wear bright or reflective clothing.
Change lanes frequently.
Focus only on your riding, not on your surroundings.

questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers. This lowers your risk of being hit. Always stay aware of other drivers and what they are doing.

questions.question: It can be difficult to ride right after it starts raining because:

options.text: Some other drivers may not react quickly enough to the rain.
Pavement will be especially slippery.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the pavement becomes very slippery. Oil from vehicles mixes with water on the road surface, creating a slick layer.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Maintain an adequate space cushion.
Ride very slowly.
Ride the centerline.

questions.explanation: Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle at all times. Maintain this space when following other vehicles, being followed, passing, or being passed.

questions.question: You have an improved chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear:

options.text: Face or eye protection.
A baseball cap.
Sneakers.

questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection in a crash. A plastic face shield protects your face from injury.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Only ride in the left portion of the lane to better see around other vehicles ahead.
Ride closely to the vehicle in front of you to most effectively use their headlights.
Reduce your speed to increase your chances of avoiding an unexpected hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to increase your chances of avoiding an unexpected hazard.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is not a danger.
Can cause irreversible hearing damage.
Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when riding. Good ear protection lets you still hear important sounds like sirens and horns.

questions.question: If vehicles are present on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually the best option?

options.text: Left
Right
Center

questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. Good riders adjust their position based on road and traffic conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually safest.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle that is stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle. Slow down and be ready to stop. Give emergency vehicles extra space when their lights are flashing.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always wear a jacket.
Wear a jacket only at night.
Wear a jacket only when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves every time you ride. Do this even if the weather is warm.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When using saddlebags to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Load both bags with equal weight.
Put more weight in one bag than the other.
Put as much weight as possible in one bag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load both bags with equal weight.
questions.explanation: Saddlebags should have about the same weight in each bag. Uneven weight can cause the motorcycle to tilt to one side.

questions.question: Keeping space between you and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can draft better off other vehicles.
You can stop faster.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you more time to see problems coming and more room to move safely.
